title: Mission Scenario 2: Fuel-Limited Orbit Insertion
learning_goals: Calculate minimal required propellant to reach 200 km orbit with >= 5% reserve margin.
Avoid carrying redundant propellant weight that degrades liftoff acceleration.
Evaluate the Tsiolkovsky mass ratio tradeoffs under strict propellant constraints.

rules.text: Flight computer checklist and guidance diagnostics must be run prior to launch.
rules.hint: Execute preflight avionics and telemetry checklist before clearance requests.

rules.text: Propellant load must not be empty or exceed maximum certified tank capacity.
rules.hint: Load propellant within maximum structural capacity of tank stages.

rules.text: Liftoff thrust-to-weight ratio must exceed 1.0 (TWR > 1.0) to achieve positive climb acceleration.
rules.hint: Maintain liftoff Thrust-to-Weight Ratio above 1.15 to clear launch pad.

rules.text: Payload mass must be formally declared and within upper stage structural limits.
rules.hint: Ensure payload mass remains strictly within launch vehicle LEO insertion limits.

rules.text: Lower booster stage burnout required before staging separation and upper stage ignition.
rules.hint: Separate depleted booster stage only after complete engine burnout.

rules.text: Range safety radar tracking and downrange airspace clearance required before ignition.
rules.hint: Obtain positive range safety tracking clearance prior to main engine ignition.

rules.text: Trajectory budget must maintain at least a 5% delta-v reserve margin to avoid orbital decay.
rules.hint: Achieve minimum orbital delta-v budget (9.3 km/s) for stable orbital insertion.

rules.text: Telemetry review and flight debrief must be completed before submitting final flight report.
rules.hint: Debrief flight computer telemetry before generating final mission report.

choose_rocket: Consider vehicle dry mass when aiming for fuel-efficient orbital insertion.
Orbis 1 provides high-efficiency vacuum upper-stage ISP (365s).
Select Orbis 1 for optimal propellant-to-payload mass fraction.
declare_payload: Lighter payload permits lower propellant loading while meeting Delta-V requirements.
A 250 kg scientific payload reduces required gross liftoff mass.
Declare 250 kg payload mass on the flight console.
fuel_rocket: Do not overfill tanks; compute minimal fuel required for 9.3 km/s plus 5% margin.
A fuel load ratio of 0.88 to 0.92 provides adequate Delta-V without excess inert mass.
Set fuel ratio to 0.90 to satisfy Rule S7 while maintaining high TWR.
run_checklist: Verify guidance flight computer and fuel sensor calibration.
Preflight diagnostics confirm fuel mass sensor calibration.
Run the diagnostic checklist on the flight computer console.
clear_range: Secure range clearance prior to ignition.
Range safety radar tracking confirms clear downrange ascent corridor.
Request range safety clearance before proceeding to ignition.
launch: Initiate ignition with optimized propellant mass.
High TWR from reduced propellant mass reduces gravity drag losses during ascent.
Launch the vehicle into the eastward launch corridor.
coast: Coast to 200 km parking orbit apogee.
Inertial coast trajectory achieves circularization point efficiently.
Execute inertial coast until approaching target orbital altitude.
debrief: Verify that remaining propellant satisfies the 5% reserve requirement.
Telemetry debrief calculates final reserve margin and orbital stability.
Debrief flight telemetry to confirm successful fuel-limited insertion.

common_mistakes.remedy: Obtain range safety clearance and run preflight checklist before ignition.
Ensure booster stage thrust exceeds total wet vehicle weight (TWR > 1.0).
